conviction_note: The findings add up to +1.7, carried by the Lincoln Tech read-across and a low bar after a 56% drawdown. The scaled number is -0.56 (p_up 48 x abs 14). That reflects UTI's reaction history: 5 of 7 prints down, and the last two guide events (initial FY26 guide Nov 2025 -20.45%, FY26 cut Aug 2026 -34.22%) were sold whatever the quarter did. It also reflects a 22-point put skew. Tomorrow's move is the first FY27 guide, and its EPS bar ($0.71) looks stretched against management's own 'modest EBITDA growth' framework. The gap between the two numbers is a quarter likely to clear (peer evidence) against a guide likely to disappoint (framework arithmetic). Neither is decisive, so p_up sits near 50 and abs_move stays large.

next_guide.street_next_quarter: Q1 FY27 (Dec 2026) EPS $0.17, 2 analysts, range $0.13-0.20, one downward revision in 4 weeks (https://therighttrader.com/earnings-calendar/uti)

next_guide.company_current_guide: No formal FY27 guide. Framework from the Q3 call (2026-08-05): FY27 revenue growth to exceed FY26 growth (about 7.3% at the FY26 guide midpoint) and modest adj EBITDA growth; FY29 targets of more than $1.2B revenue and adj EBITDA approaching $220M; three to four FY27 campus openings; FY26 capex about $110M (https://www.themarketsdaily.com/?p=9889007 as quoted in search results; FY26 guide from the 8-K exhibit).
next_guide.basis: Revenue: the framework implies at least $962M, so the street's $969M is roughly at the guide. EPS: the framework is modest EBITDA growth on a $100-103M base, while D&A rises from about $110M of capex and new revolver usage. That makes the street's +17% EPS ($0.605 to $0.71) look high, and the street is already revising down. Last November the initial FY guide came below the street and the stock fell 20%.

findings.finding: Lincoln Tech (LINC) is the closest listed peer: the same auto/diesel/skilled-trades programs, the same high-school recruiting channel, and the same Jul-Sep quarter as UTI's fiscal Q4. On 2026-11-09 it reported Q3 starts +14.2% (7,362), Transportation & Skilled Trades starts +16.5% and healthcare +4.2%. It credited better lead-to-start conversion and expanded high-school outreach, and raised FY revenue guidance to $600-605M. UTI cut its guide in August because Q4 high-school auto/diesel starts were tracking below plan, which it blamed on field staffing rather than demand. The peer confirms channel demand was strong in the very quarter UTI is reporting, which makes a starts miss beyond the narrowed 31,900-32,300 range less likely.
findings.link: Same programs (automotive, diesel, skilled trades: 6,120 of LINC's 7,362 Q3 starts), the same high-school channel UTI named as its problem, and the same calendar quarter (Jul-Sep 2026). LINC revenue is about $600M a year against UTI's about $900M. UTI's division is about 63% of revenue (Q3: $138.0M of $218.9M).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: UTI rose +10.1% on 2026-11-09 (19.93 to 21.95) and another +5.7% on 11-10 on LINC's print. It has since given back to 22.27, against 23.21 on 11-10. Starts were the line of the Aug 2026 -34% guide cut.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. UTI added about 16% over 11-09/11-10 but has given back about 4% since and trades at its 11-04 level, so the stock absorbed the peer print only as far as undoing the unexplained 11-05 sector drop. If the read-across were fully in the price, UTI would hold above its 11-10 high of 23.21 and short interest would be falling. Instead it rose to 14.0% at the 10-30 settlement.
findings.independence: The webull/Barchart summary (https://www.webull.com/news/15898763961233408) gives the same LINC data and says management credits high-school recruiting investment. UTI's own Q3 release reports UTI-division starts +23.4% and Atlanta starts 30% ahead of plan. These come from different issuers.

findings.finding: First FY27 guide risk. On the Q3 call (2026-08-05) management framed FY27 as revenue growth above FY26's (about 7.3%) with only 'modest' adj EBITDA growth from a $100-103M FY26 base. Capex of about $110M and three to four new campuses (Salt Lake City, Houston, Phoenix, Concorde-Atlanta in summer 2027) raise D&A. The street's FY27 EPS of $0.71 (4 analysts, range $0.64-0.76) is +17% on the $0.605 FY26 guide midpoint, and its FY27 revenue of $969M is +8.1%. An EPS guide starting near $0.60-0.68 would sit below the street, as the initial FY26 guide did in November 2025.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The initial FY26 guide on 2025-11-19 came with a Q4 beat and EBITDA/earnings guidance below expectations; the stock fell 20.45% (baseline; https://rallies.ai/news/universal-technical-institute-q4-beat-vs-below-forecast-2026-guidance-sparks-selloff). The FY26 cut on 2026-08-05 drew -34.22%. The guide line has decided the last two big moves.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The stock is 56% off its high and the put skew is +22 points. But the FY27 EPS consensus has barely moved (one downward revision in 4 weeks) and still implies +17% EPS on modest EBITDA growth. If the market fully expected a guide below the street, sell-side numbers would already have come down toward the framework.
findings.independence: Street figures come from https://therighttrader.com/earnings-calendar/uti and https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/uti/forecast/. The capex and campus plan comes from the Q3 8-K exhibit. The framework quote is a secondary summary of the call (that page now returns 404; it was quoted in search results), so this is inference from management's framework, not a document of the guide. The bar is single-source aggregators, so the finding is capped.

findings.finding: The Q4 consensus (EPS $0.33, revenue $235.0-235.7M) sits at the midpoint of what the cut FY26 guide implies for Q4: revenue $231.9-238.9M and EPS $0.29-0.36. The guide was set on 2026-08-05, when the summer high-school start cohort was already visible. UTI beat EPS consensus in Q1 FY26 ($0.23 vs about $0.14) and in Q3, so an in-line-to-modest beat on the quarter is the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Quarter beats have been sold. Q3 FY26 was a beat and fell -34.22%; Q4 FY25 was a beat and fell -20.45%; Q1 FY26 was a beat and fell -11.16%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The consensus is the guide midpoint, and the finding lands inside what the company guided. Only a beat beyond $0.36 or $239M would be new information.
findings.independence: The Q1 EPS beat is from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1261654/000126165426000003/exhibit991-q12026earningsp.htm. The Q3 beat headline is from https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/UTI.

findings.finding: Expectations are already low. Spot of $22.42 is 56% below the 52-week high, -29.6% since the August release, and 42% below the lowest sell-side target ($30; mean $38.33 from 6 analysts). Targets were cut in the quarter: Texas Capital to Hold at $25 (09-21), Barrington to $30 (10-01). Bearish sentiment readings doubled to 48.4%. The real bar for the quarter and guide is therefore below the consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean precedent in the baseline. The last four prints all fell (-34.22, -3.98, -11.16, -20.45), but they came from higher levels (about $40 before Q3).
findings.why_not_priced: A low bar is by definition partly in the price. What is not priced is the asymmetry: a guide merely in line with the framework, against a stock priced well below the most bearish target, gives room for relief. If this were priced, the put skew would not be +22 points.
findings.independence: Sentiment readings and the drop since the last print are from https://finviz.com/news/420785/uti-must-prove-its-guidance-cut-was-an-execution-stumble-not-a-demand-problem. Price levels are from the Yahoo chart.

findings.finding: Short interest rose every settlement from 5.06M (9.2% of 55.1M shares) on 2026-08-14 to 7.69M (14.0%, 5.52 days to cover) on 2026-10-30. Shorts built into the print, which makes the downside a consensus trade and sets up a squeeze if the FY27 guide is merely in line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not observed on this name. Short interest was about 10% at the August print, which still fell 34%.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the market's view, not unpriced information. The finding is the mechanism: a rising short at 5.5 days to cover on 1.36M average volume amplifies an upside surprise. The finding is small because rising shorts may themselves be informed.
findings.independence: The sweep row cites the same equibles figure, so this is not independent. The baseline put skew points the other way (downside paid).

findings.why_not_priced: The purchases are small (about $310k in total) from one director, so they barely register. Buying through September, inside the quarter being reported, is weak evidence that nothing worse was known internally.
findings.independence: Other Form 4s from the same director: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1261654/000119312526347428/0001193125-26-347428.txt and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1261654/000119312526371793/0001193125-26-371793.txt. The same person, so one finding.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-12 UTI replaced its $125M Fifth Third revolver with a $200M secured revolver maturing 2031 (SOFR+1.50-2.25%, plus a $75M accordion). The money funds the campus build-out (capex about $110M, adjusted FCF guide -$20M to $0). Early ramp evidence: Atlanta starts 30% ahead of plan and San Antonio ahead of its launch model. Financing funds visible demand, so this is a small positive.
findings.why_not_priced: The facility is public. The point is the sign: it corroborates the FY27 campus ramp rather than distress, and the leverage covenants leave room.
findings.independence: The Q3 8-K exhibit gives the Atlanta and San Antonio starts tracking.

findings.finding: On 2026-11-05 UTI fell 11.8% (22.33 to 19.69) on the same day as LINC (-12.7%) and PRDO (-11.5%). No cause was found in news or filings, and UTI has since fully recovered to about the 11-04 level. That points to an unexplained sector-wide shock to post-secondary for-profit names inside the quarter's run-in.
findings.why_not_priced: Unexplained; an absent cause is worth 0. It is filed so the judges see that the sector carries a shared, unexplained shock risk.
findings.independence: The same move is in the LINC chart (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/LINC?range=1mo&interval=1d) and the PRDO chart (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/PRDO?range=1mo&interval=1d).

findings.finding: Regulatory backdrop. ED's earnings-accountability framework (proposed 2026-04-20; reportedly finalised 2026-07-01) extends an earnings test to undergraduate certificate programs, with the earliest loss of loan eligibility on 2028-07-01. On 2026-08-26 ED threatened aid cuts for institutions missing the Oct 1 program-data reporting deadline. Nothing UTI-specific was found, and the consequences fall after the window.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and long-dated. It matters only if management quantifies program exposure on the call.

baseline_tension: Partly against. The peer read and the low bar lean up against a +22-point put skew and a reaction history of 5 of 7 down. The next-guide risk agrees with the skew. p_up sits at 48 rather than leaning either way.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (crowded short, 14% and 5.5 days to cover) and rule 6 (FY27 bar from single aggregator sources) shrank the next_guide negative from -2.5 to -1.5.
Rule 1 (beats sold on this name) shrank the Q4 consensus_bar finding from +0.5 to +0.3.
Rule 9 (net of the UTI division's +23% starts) shrank the Concorde finding from -0.5 to -0.3.
Rule 3 and the core table moved p_up from 47 to 48 because the evidence cuts against the skew; abs_move left at 14 for the first FY27 guide.

Rule 5 confirmed the unexplained 11-05 sector drop at 0. Rule 4 left the revolver at +0.2 after asking what it funds. The 'peer print after the company last spoke' pattern left the LINC finding at +1.5.
